text.p: Steffi Graf was released on Wednesday from the Vienna hospital where she underwent knee surgery and headed for a private physiotherapy clinic to start what is expected to be a lengthy period of recuperation.
A spokeswoman at the Willy Dungl Clinic in Gars am Kamp, 60 kms northwest of the Austrian capital, said Graf was due to arrive later on Wednesday, adding "We do not know how long she will stay."
Graf has been a regular visitor to the clinic which in the past has treated such sports stars as former Formula One driver Niki Lauda and the late Ayrton Senna.

The 27-year-old German former world number one and winner of 21 grand slam titles was released from hospital only 24 hours after doctor Reinhard Weinstabl had operated on her left knee at an undisclosed private hospital in Vienna.
Doctors expect she will be unable to compete for another four to six months, which would rule her out of both remaining grand slam tournaments this year.

In a statement issued by the Women's Tennis Association on Tuesday, Graf expressed her deep disappointment at being unable to defend her Wimbledon title and said her participation in the U.S. Open was also unlikely.
"When exactly I will be able to compete again is not clear. The doctors told me that with extensive physiotherapy, returning in four to six months is realistic.
"I am confident that I will be able to return to the game I love so much -- this time healthy," said Graf, adding she had experienced pain during last week's French Open.
Graf, who slipped to number three in the world rankings after being knocked out of the quarter-finals in Paris by Amanda Coetzer, first suffered the injury at Wimbledon last year.
The seven times Wimbledon champion said the injury was identified during magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) which showed a cartilage fracture and partial rupture of a tendon.
She already had arthroscopic surgery in February after defaulting from a tournament in Tokyo and was hampered by an infected toe at the Australian Open in January.
Wimbledon starts on June 23 and the U.S. Open begins on August 25.
